causal:influence:motor_neuron_firing_rat.mechanism: Higher motor neuron action potential firing rates activate more motor units (size principle: small, low-threshold units fire at lower frequencies; as firing rate increases, larger motor units are progressively recruited). Each recruited unit adds its muscle fibers to the active pool, increasing the total number of recruited motor units.

causal:influence:motor_unit_recruitment:.evidence: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-056 (10.5: Nervous System Control of Muscle Tension): motor unit recruitment and summation underlie gradation of muscle force including resting tone. Guyton & Hall Medical Physiology Ch. 55: spinal reflex arcs maintaining muscle tone; lower motor neuron lesions → flaccid paralysis (zero tone); upper motor neuron lesions → hypertonicity (increased recruitment). | intervention: mechanistic model: lower motor neuron block (do(motor_unit_recruitment=0)) causes flaccid paralysis (no tone); baclofen (GABA-B agonist reducing motor neuron firing, do(recruitment↓)) decreases spastic tone clinically
causal:influence:motor_unit_recruitment:.mechanism: Resting skeletal muscle tone is maintained by a low level of tonic motor unit activity (low-frequency, asynchronous firing of a small fraction of motor units). Higher motor unit recruitment increases the number of active fibers contributing to resting tone. Loss of lower motor neuron input (e.g. lower motor neuron lesion) abolishes tone (flaccid paralysis); increased input (e.g. upper motor neuron lesion) increases tonic recruitment and raises tone (spasticity).

NH3 produced in contracting muscle enters the circulation, contributing to post-exercise rise in plasma ammonia. In AMPD1 deficiency, the post-exercise plasma ammonia rise is markedly attenuated or absent. More AMPD1 activity increases muscle ammonia production and thereby raises plasma ammonia during exercise.

Interaction (two-factor interventional cross-term): Martiszus, Tsintsadze, Chang & Smith, 'Enhanced excitability of cortical neurons in low-divalent solutions is primarily mediated by altered voltage-dependence of voltage-gated sodium channels', eLife 2021;10:e67914 (VERIFIED via WebSearch, elifesciences.org/articles/67914; authors confirmed). Switching the bath from physiological to reduced extracellular divalent/Ca2+ (a do() on [Ca2+]o) left-shifted Na+-channel V0.5, increasing channel availability and the efficacy of a given depolarisation -> enhanced excitability; thus the SLOPE of the depolarising-input -> firing relation changes with [Ca2+]o (the required gain cross-term). Foundation: Frankenhaeuser & Hodgkin 1957 (surface-charge screening). Textbook anchors: Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (low plasma Ca2+ raises neuromuscular excitability -> tetany); Boron & Boulpaep, Medical Physiology (membrane potential / hypocalcaemic tetany). Sign: d(gain)/d([Ca2+]o) < 0 (membrane stabilisation), monotonic screening so can_flip_sign=false. [NB: first-order additive shadow (plasma_calcium -> postsynaptic_membrane_potential) is not currently in the causal graph, so only the second-order gain query is represented; sound (adds no node-level prediction).]
modulation:modulation-d3e544744c53d23b34.mechanism: Extracellular (plasma, ionised) Ca2+ screens the fixed negative surface charges on the outer membrane face and on voltage-gated Na+ channels (Frankenhaeuser-Hodgkin surface-potential effect). Raising [Ca2+]o increases screening, right-shifting (depolarising) the voltage-dependence of Na+-channel activation, so a given excitatory (ACh) synaptic drive moves the cell less far toward firing threshold. The gain of the depolarising-input -> membrane-potential/excitability edge therefore FALLS as [Ca2+]o rises (membrane-stabilising action; hypercalcaemia -> hypoexcitability) and RISES in hypocalcaemia (latent tetany / Chvostek-Trousseau). This is a genuine multiplicative gain on the depolarising input, not an additive push on membrane potential.
